  if n ≤ 1 then n else

def sqrt (n : Nat) : Nat :=
  if n ≤ 1 then n else
  iter n (n / 2)

def sqrt (n : Nat) : Nat :=
  if n ≤ 1 then n else
  iter n (n / 2)

  if n ≤ 1 then n else

/--
Integer square root function. Implemented via Newton's method.
-/
def sqrt (n : Nat) : Nat :=
  if n ≤ 1 then n else
  iter n (n / 2)
where
  /-- Auxiliary for `sqrt`. If `guess` is greater than the integer square root of `n`,
  returns the integer square root of `n`. -/
  iter (n guess : Nat) : Nat :=
    let next := (guess + n / guess) / 2
    if _h : next < guess then
      iter n next
    else
      guess
  termination_by guess

/--
Integer square root function. Implemented via Newton's method.
-/
def sqrt (n : Nat) : Nat :=
  if n ≤ 1 then n else
  iter n (n / 2)
where

  returns the integer square root of `n`. -/
  iter (n guess : Nat) : Nat :=
    let next := (guess + n / guess) / 2
    if _h : next < guess then
      iter n next
    else
      guess
  termination_by guess

def sqrt (n : Nat) : Nat :=
  if n ≤ 1 then n else
  iter n (n / 2)

  returns the integer square root of `n`. -/
  iter (n guess : Nat) : Nat :=

    if _h : next < guess then

    else

def sqrt (n : Nat) : Nat :=
  if n ≤ 1 then n else
  iter n (n / 2)

    else

  if n ≤ 1 then n else

/--
Integer square root function. Implemented via Newton's method.
-/
def sqrt (n : Nat) : Nat :=
  if n ≤ 1 then n else
  iter n (n / 2)
where
  /-- Auxiliary for `sqrt`. If `guess` is greater than the integer square root of `n`,
  returns the integer square root of `n`. -/
  iter (n guess : Nat) : Nat :=
    let next := (guess + n / guess) / 2
    if _h : next < guess then
      iter n next
    else
      guess
  termination_by guess

/--
Integer square root function. Implemented via Newton's method.
-/
def sqrt (n : Nat) : Nat :=
  if n ≤ 1 then n else
  iter n (n / 2)
where
  /-- Auxiliary for `sqrt`. If `guess` is greater than the integer square root of `n`,
  returns the integer square root of `n`. -/
  iter (n guess : Nat) : Nat :=

    if _h : next < guess then
      iter n next
    else

same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.

`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is

`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is

same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

    ∃ (a : _) (_ : a ∈ Finset.Icc n (2 * n) \ A) (b : _) (_ : b ∈ Finset.Icc n (2 * n) \ A),

  -- such that all pairwise sums are perfect squares. In practice, it will be easier to use
  -- a finite set B ⊆ [n, 2n] such that all pairwise unequal pairs of B sum to a perfect square
  -- noting that B has cardinality greater or equal to 3, by the explicit construction of the
  -- triplet {a, b, c} before.

  have hBsub : B ⊆ Finset.Icc n (2 * n) := by

    exact Nat.succ_le_iff.mp hB

  -- for any A ⊆ [n, 2n], either C ⊆ A or C ⊆ [n, 2n] \ A and C has cardinality greater
  -- or equal to 2.

  -- such that all pairwise sums are perfect squares. In practice, it will be easier to use

theorem subset_iff {s₁ s₂ : Finset α} : s₁ ⊆ s₂ ↔ ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ s₁ → x ∈ s₂ :=

--name=Finset.one_lt_card
--context_item_type=theorem
theorem one_lt_card : 1 < #s ↔ ∃ a ∈ s, ∃ b ∈ s, a ≠ b := by
  rw [← not_iff_not]
  push_neg
  exact card_le_one
</ITEM>

theorem exists_subset_or_subset_of_two_mul_lt_card [DecidableEq α] {X Y : Finset α} {n : ℕ}
    (hXY : 2 * n < #(X ∪ Y)) : ∃ C : Finset α, n < #C ∧ (C ⊆ X ∨ C ⊆ Y) := by
  have h₁ : #(X ∩ (Y \ X)) = 0 := Finset.card_eq_zero.mpr (Finset.inter_sdiff_self X Y)
  have h₂ : #(X ∪ Y) = #X + #(Y \ X) := by
    rw [← card_union_add_card_inter X (Y \ X), Finset.union_sdiff_self_eq_union, h₁, add_zero]
  rw [h₂, Nat.two_mul] at hXY
  obtain h | h : n < #X ∨ n < #(Y \ X) := by contrapose! hXY; omega
  · exact ⟨X, h, Or.inl (Finset.Subset.refl X)⟩
  · exact ⟨Y \ X, h, Or.inr sdiff_subset⟩

    (∃ (a : _) (_ : a ∈ A) (b : _) (_ : b ∈ A), a ≠ b ∧ ∃ k : ℕ, a + b = k ^ 2) ∨
    ∃ (a : _) (_ : a ∈ Finset.Icc n (2 * n) \ A) (b : _) (_ : b ∈ Finset.Icc n (2 * n) \ A),
      a ≠ b ∧ ∃ k : ℕ, a + b = k ^ 2 := by
  intro n hn A hA

  -- such that all pairwise sums are perfect squares. In practice, it will be easier to use
  -- a finite set B ⊆ [n, 2n] such that all pairwise unequal pairs of B sum to a perfect square
  -- noting that B has cardinality greater or equal to 3, by the explicit construction of the
  -- triplet {a, b, c} before.

  have hBsub : B ⊆ Finset.Icc n (2 * n) := by
    intro c hcB; simpa only [Finset.mem_Icc] using h₂ c hcB
  have hB' : 2 * 1 < (B ∩ (Finset.Icc n (2 * n) \ A) ∪ B ∩ A).card := by
    rw [←inter_union_distrib_left, sdiff_union_self_eq_union, union_eq_left.2 hA,
      inter_eq_left.2 hBsub]
    exact Nat.succ_le_iff.mp hB

  -- for any A ⊆ [n, 2n], either C ⊆ A or C ⊆ [n, 2n] \ A and C has cardinality greater
  -- or equal to 2.

    (∃ (a : _) (_ : a ∈ A) (b : _) (_ : b ∈ A), a ≠ b ∧ ∃ k : ℕ, a + b = k ^ 2) ∨
    ∃ (a : _) (_ : a ∈ Finset.Icc n (2 * n) \ A) (b : _) (_ : b ∈ Finset.Icc n (2 * n) \ A),
      a ≠ b ∧ ∃ k : ℕ, a + b = k ^ 2 := by

  -- such that all pairwise sums are perfect squares. In practice, it will be easier to use
  -- a finite set B ⊆ [n, 2n] such that all pairwise unequal pairs of B sum to a perfect square
  -- noting that B has cardinality greater or equal to 3, by the explicit construction of the
  -- triplet {a, b, c} before.
  obtain ⟨B, hB, h₁, h₂⟩ := exists_finset_3_le_card_with_pairs_summing_to_squares n hn
  have hBsub : B ⊆ Finset.Icc n (2 * n) := by
    intro c hcB; simpa only [Finset.mem_Icc] using h₂ c hcB
  have hB' : 2 * 1 < (B ∩ (Finset.Icc n (2 * n) \ A) ∪ B ∩ A).card := by
    rw [←inter_union_distrib_left, sdiff_union_self_eq_union, union_eq_left.2 hA,
      inter_eq_left.2 hBsub]
    exact Nat.succ_le_iff.mp hB
  -- Since B has cardinality greater or equal to 3, there must exist a subset C ⊆ B such that
  -- for any A ⊆ [n, 2n], either C ⊆ A or C ⊆ [n, 2n] \ A and C has cardinality greater
  -- or equal to 2.
  obtain ⟨C, hC, hCA⟩ := Finset.exists_subset_or_subset_of_two_mul_lt_card hB'
  rw [Finset.one_lt_card] at hC
  rcases hC with ⟨a, ha, b, hb, hab⟩
  simp only [Finset.subset_iff, Finset.mem_inter] at hCA
  -- Now we split into the two cases C ⊆ [n, 2n] \ A and C ⊆ A, which can be dealt with identically.
  cases' hCA with hCA hCA <;> [right; left] <;>
    exact ⟨a, (hCA ha).2, b, (hCA hb).2, hab, h₁ a (hCA ha).1 b (hCA hb).1 hab⟩
